title: Getting interim relief from court before arbitration even begins
p1:
What if your business is facing immediate damage, but the arbitration process hasn't even started yet?

Many people assume they must wait for the arbitrator to be appointed before asking for protection.
p2:
That is a common misconception. In many cases, courts can grant urgent temporary protection even before arbitration begins.

This is called interim relief — a legal safeguard to prevent assets from being hidden, evidence from being destroyed, or a situation from becoming impossible to reverse.
p3:
For example, if a party is about to sell disputed property or transfer money to avoid future claims, approaching the court early can help preserve the situation until the arbitration moves forward.

The key insight: arbitration does not always mean waiting. Courts can step in when immediate action is needed, even before the main dispute resolution process starts.
conclusion: Did you know a court can sometimes protect your rights before an arbitrator even hears the case? Would you seek interim relief in such a situation?
